text.p: Shares in McKechnie Plc dropped on Wednesday, reversing yesterday's gains despite results showing a sharp rise in first-half profits coupled with a mostly postive trading statement.
"People were getting excited ahead of the results and the stock ran ahead of itself, we've seen a bit of profit-taking today but it's still quite solid," said one market-maker in the stock.
McKechnie shares were 19p lower at 545p by 0950 GMT, having risen 15p on Tuesday.
The engineering plastics and metal components group reported a 36 percent rise in first-half pre-tax profits to 28.1 million stg, which traders said was broadly in line with expectations.
The group said trading in the second half had started well and it looked forward to "further satisfactory progress" despite the stronger pound affecting overseas earnings.

"The significant strengthening of sterling is affecting the translation of overseas earnings and export margins, but the British construction and DIY markets, which account for 17 percent of our sales, are showing signs of recovery," McKechnie said in a statement.
It warned it would also incur a one-off cost of not more than $6.5 million this year to terminate a major loss-making contract.
